nodes.name: Receive Inbound Webhook
nodes.notes: Entry point: listens for POST calls on /wf03312-document. Use the TEST url while building, switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after publishing. Watch out: While building use the TEST url; switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after you publish.

nodes.name: Read Recent from Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Document Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Trim to Digest Size
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 15 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Summarize Content (AI)
nodes.notes: Map-reduce summarization chain — handles long content without blowing the context window.

nodes.name: OpenRouter Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: OpenRouter API key. openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.

nodes.name: Render as HTML
nodes.notes: Converts markdown to HTML for rich rendering in email/CMS.

nodes.name: Post Digest to Microsoft Teams
nodes.notes: Posts a chat message into a Microsoft Teams channel — same role as a Slack notify, for teams standardized on Teams. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.

nodes.name: Archive Digest in Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Document Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

parameters.content:
# Digest long emails with Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams automatically

**Pattern:** AI Summarize & Route · **Level:** Foundation · **Trigger:** Webhook

## What it does
Digest long emails with Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams automatically. It fires the moment an external system calls its webhook.

## Why it exists
Manual summarization is slow and error-prone; this workflow makes the process repeatable, monitored and hands-off, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow
Receive Inbound Webhook → Read Recent from Google Sheets → Newest First → Trim to Digest Size → Summarize Content (AI) → Render as HTML → Post Digest to Microsoft Teams → …

## Use it for
- Teams that want to ai summarize & route without manual effort
- Anyone automating summarization in legal
- Replacing a fragile manual process with a reliable workflow

## You get
- Scales without extra headcount
- Has retries and error handling built in
- Standardizes the process every time

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; OpenRouter API key.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Summarization uses a Chain, not an Agent, because the step is fixed — there's no decision about which tool to call, just 'summarize this text.' Posting to multiple channels runs as parallel branches, not sequential sends, so a slow API on one channel never delays the message that was already ready on another.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Add a third notification channel and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Change 'Trim to Digest Size' from 15 to 5 and see how it narrows the summary's scope.
3. Swap the Summarization Chain for a Q&A Chain to answer questions instead of just recapping.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**OpenRouter API key**
openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.
_Gotcha:_ One key reaches many models — handy for fallback.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🔐 Security

Never trust inbound payloads: the webhook path is unguessable. Add header auth or IP allow-listing for defense in depth. Secrets live in n8n credentials — never in node parameters.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your summarization process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
